revision: not recorded here — a manifest cannot name the commit that contains it, for the same reason it cannot contain its own hash. The release identity is version + revision + digest: two are in-tree, and the consuming project records the revision in its own pin and verifies with `pack_pin.py <root> --version <v> --sha <full-40-char-rev> --digest <d> --state <state>`. See docs/RP2.2-GATE.md.
digest_note: release-local framing. Verify a release with the tools/pack_pin.py that ships inside it; a manifest naming an algorithm the verifier does not implement fails as a version mismatch, not as tampering.
supersedes: 2.1.1 — not replaced; runs pinned to it stay pinned to it. 2.1.1, 2.1.0 and 2.0.0 histories are untouched. This candidate is IN_PROGRESS and no project may adopt it: QUALIFIED_AND_FROZEN is the only adoptable state.
version_semantics: PATCH: backward-compatible fixes, metadata/docs corrections, enforcement of already-promised guarantees. MINOR: new backward-compatible policy/tool/capability. MAJOR: incompatible authority, contract or migration change. VERSION is the single machine-readable authority (DECISIONS.md D11).
pin_instruction: a project records ROOT PATH and version and full 40-character sha and tree digest and state in PROJECT.yaml pack.*, and verifies them rather than copying them. All four identity fields are required: `root_path` says WHICH DIRECTORY, the other three say WHAT is in it, and a pin without the root is UNVERIFIABLE_LEGACY_PIN (tools/pack_migration.py) because the release it names cannot be identified. Adoption happens only at a capability boundary. A frozen release never mutates during a project run; verification failing mid-project is a stop, not a pin to refresh.
concurrent_use: several projects may pin this same release at once, or different qualified releases, provided each version resolves to a distinct immutable root. Operational state and Evolution Candidate inboxes are project-local and never written into this repository (DECISIONS.md D13).

external_installed_skills.authority: ADAPTERS, NOT AUTHORITY. Outside this release envelope, covered by no tree_digest_sha256, and changeable without a pin noticing. Where an adapter and this pinned pack disagree, the pinned pack wins. From 2.2.0 an adapter a project dispatches through is DECLARED AND VERIFIED under the project's own adapters contract (tools/adapter_pin.py, PROJECT.yaml `adapters:`) — this list is an observation of what was installed here, never a substitute for that declaration (DECISIONS.md D12, D14).

known_limitations: STATE IS IN_PROGRESS. This candidate has not been released by a human authority and no project may pin it.

NO CLOSURE AUDIT ROUND HAS RETURNED READY. Four rounds ran, eight blind auditors on distinct lenses, and every round returned NOT READY. Each round's findings were reproduced and repaired and the next round found more, including in the repairs. The last round's findings are repaired and unaudited. docs/RP2.2-GATE.md records each round. Four closure cycles were the authorised budget and four ran, so a fifth round is what remains rather than a smaller step. Because the fourth round's central finding was repairs with no oracle, every repair in the closing batch was mutation-tested before commit: five mutations, all killed.

A REPAIR REGRESSED THE COMMIT GATE against the qualified 2.1.1 baseline, more than once, before the guarantee was pinned by an absolute property test rather than by a differential. The regressions are closed; that they happened is the more useful fact.

CROSS-VENDOR AUDIT WAS NOT AVAILABLE in any round. The final-gate tier asks for two blind auditors with one cross-vendor WHERE AVAILABLE; two ran each round, within one family. The measured value of the tier - that the two populations come back almost disjoint - was obtained, but not across vendors.

SEVERAL CLAIMS ARE UNFALSIFIABLE FROM THIS REPOSITORY and are marked so in the gate record: the four adapter digests and both adapter repairs (outside the envelope, and the pre-repair originals were not retained), the Project Context file count (in another project), and the status-line payload schema (read from the installed client, no artifact shipped). resource_observation.py has been exercised against constructed payloads and never a live one.
the tree digest is computed over WORKING-TREE BYTES, so a checkout with core.autocrlf=true produces a different digest for the same commit. There is no .gitattributes.

PROSE CLAIMS ABOUT THIS RELEASE'S OWN HISTORY ARE CHECKED BY A READER, NOT BY A TEST. Two guards cover the two lies that actually recurred - no document may state a pathmatch divergence figure, and every count in the derived routing view must match policy/observations.jsonl - but they are not the general case. A sentence in docs/RP2.2-RELEASE-PACKET.md that misdescribed what an audit found would ship green. On four rounds' evidence this is the likeliest remaining defect in the candidate.

THIS RELEASE WAS NOT EXERCISED AGAINST A REAL CONSUMER UNTIL AFTER THE AUDIT BUDGET CLOSED, and the first pass found three defects: one made a live project's PROJECT.yaml unreadable by every tool, one answered about a project whose contract had never been opened, and one made every tool print a stack trace where it should have reported a refusal. Both are repaired and mutation-tested. What is not established is whether the rest of the toolbelt behaves against real project data as it does against fixtures: one pass found two, and nothing says a second would find none. See docs/RP2.2-GATE.md, 'After the audit budget closed'.

NOT PUBLIC-SAFE BY CONSTRUCTION YET. Ten occurrences of private project names remain in four files inherited from the frozen 2.1.1 baseline (docs/WAVE-B-GATE.md, docs/RP2.1-DELTA-AUDIT.md, docs/RP2.1-GATE.md, policy/observations.jsonl). They are historical evidence and were deliberately not rewritten. The candidate itself introduces nothing in that category, and the two things it did introduce - a real session identifier and private product names in two new documents - were found by the check and removed before commit. This is a finding for a separate publication audit; a private remote does not resolve it. See docs/RP2.2-GATE.md, 'Public-safety status of the candidate'.

THE ADAPTER PATH IS UNEXERCISED BY ANY REAL CONSUMER. None of the three real projects declares adapters, so capability_open's adapter component and adapter_pin's verification are covered by constructed fixtures only. The one adapter defect this release found was in an installed adapter file, not through a project's declaration of one.
